title: Dimpact is a federated buyer: one relationship reaches 40+ Dutch municipalities that procure software jointly
content:
Dimpact is a cooperative of more than 40 municipalities that jointly develops and procures open-source software. It built PodiumD and co-built KISS, so it is a producer as well as a buyer: the members pool requirements and engineering, not only purchasing power.

The research identifies the structure rather than the product — a federated buyer, the same shape as the Danish bank IT cooperatives noted elsewhere in the corpus. The consequence is arithmetic. One relationship reaches 40+ municipalities, so the cost of a single integration is amortised across all of them; equally, a rejection removes 40+ prospects at once.

That is why the research calls it probably the highest-leverage single conversation in the Benelux. It also implies a particular motion. Cooperatives decide collectively and slowly, and what they adopt they then maintain, so the qualifying question is whether a component can be handed over as shared infrastructure rather than whether one municipality has budget this year.
